text:
**Ra.One** is a 2011 Indian science fiction film directed by Anubhav Sinha and starring Shah Rukh Khan in a dual role as Shekhar Subramaniam, a video game programmer, and G.One, a heroic superhero character from his game. The story begins when Shekhar's colleague, Akashi, creates a new antagonist, Ra.One, a self-aware AI with shapeshifting abilities, which becomes a threat to the game's protagonist, G.One. Upon launching the game, Ra.One breaks out of the digital world into reality, killing Akashi and subsequently murdering Shekhar. The film's plot follows Shekhar's son, Prateek, and Shekhar's wife, Sonia, as they attempt to bring G.One into the real world to defeat the rogue AI. After a series of battles where G.One temporarily disables Ra.One by stealing his H.A.R.T (Health, Armor, Repair, and Time) chip, Ra.One multiplies into ten copies. G.One and Prateek eventually realize that only one of the clones possesses a shadow, allowing them to identify and destroy the real villain. In the conclusion, G.One is restored to the real world, and the characters return to London, with G.One permanently living among humans.
The film is notable for its extensive use of visual effects and its innovative title, which names the villain rather than the hero, a choice intended to highlight the rising importance of antagonists in modern cinema. Produced by Shah Rukh Khan under his banner Red Chillies Entertainment, Ra.One faced significant controversies, including allegations of plagiarism from various Hollywood franchises like Terminator 2 and the Batman series, as well as cyberattacks on its official website. Despite these challenges and mixed critical reviews regarding its plot, the film was a commercial success in India, grossing over ₹1.14 billion domestically and earning international recognition for its technical achievements, including winning the National Film Award and the Filmfare Award for Best Special Effects.
